1. Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days — adjust downward by 2–5% for the first 10 days.

2. Model underestimates late in the horizon (last 5–10 days) — increase forecast by 2–5% for the final 10 days.

3. After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 3–7% immediately after a spike, then apply gradual mean reversion.

4. Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the 10–20 day window — add 1–3% to forecast values in this range to counteract mean reversion bias.

5. Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 2–5 days — shift forecast values forward by 1–2 days in the 10–20 day window to align with actual momentum.

6. Model overreacts to recent volatility — dampen forecast sensitivity to recent 5-day price changes by applying a 0.5–1x smoothing factor to recent data points.
